title: OZEMPIC (semaglutide) injection, for subcutaneous use: full prescribing information
journal: US Food and Drug Administration; DailyMed, US National Library of Medicine, set id adec4fd2-6858-4c99-91d4-531f5f2a2d79, version 20, effective 1 June 2026
result: Initial US approval 2017. Indications: glycaemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes; reduction of major adverse cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetes with established cardiovascular disease; reduction of sustained eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease and cardiovascular death in type 2 diabetes with chronic kidney disease. Boxed warning: semaglutide causes dose- and duration-dependent thyroid C-cell adenomas and carcinomas in mice and rats at clinically relevant exposures; human relevance has not been determined; contraindicated with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2; routine calcitonin or ultrasound monitoring is of uncertain value. Warnings: acute pancreatitis, including fatal and non-fatal haemorrhagic or necrotising pancreatitis; in glycaemic trials adjudicated pancreatitis in 7 semaglutide-treated patients (0.3 per 100 patient-years) against 3 on comparators (0.2). Diabetic retinopathy complications in the 2-year SUSTAIN 6 trial 3.0% against 1.8% on placebo, 8.2% against 5.2% with retinopathy at baseline and 0.7% against 0.4% without; the effect of long-term glycaemic control on retinopathy complications has not been studied. Hypoglycaemia with a sulfonylurea: severe in 0.8% and 1.2% on 0.5 and 1 mg; with basal insulin severe in 1.5% on 1 mg against 0% on placebo over 30 weeks. Postmarketing acute kidney injury, in some cases requiring haemodialysis, mostly after nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea with dehydration. Severe gastrointestinal reactions in 0.4% (0.5 mg) and 0.8% (1 mg) against 0% on placebo; not recommended in severe gastroparesis. Anaphylaxis and angio-oedema. Cholelithiasis 1.5% (0.5 mg) and 0.4% (1 mg) against 0% on placebo. Rare postmarketing pulmonary aspiration during general anaesthesia or deep sedation with residual gastric contents despite fasting; data are insufficient to say whether modified fasting or temporary discontinuation reduces retained gastric contents. Gastrointestinal reactions in placebo-controlled trials 32.7% and 36.4% against 15.3%, leading to discontinuation in 3.1% and 3.8% against 0.4%. Mean heart rate increase 2 to 3 beats per minute. Mean lipase rise 22% and amylase 13%. Postmarketing: necrotising pancreatitis sometimes resulting in death, ileus, intestinal obstruction, severe constipation including faecal impaction, cholecystitis, cholecystectomy, acute kidney injury, alopecia. Stop at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy; in rats, rabbits and monkeys embryofetal loss and structural abnormalities occurred at clinical exposures. Mechanism: glucose-dependent stimulation of insulin and lowering of glucagon secretion, delayed early postprandial gastric emptying; the mechanism of kidney risk reduction has not been established. Half-life about 1 week; present in the circulation about 5 weeks after the last dose. In FLOW, safety data collection was limited to serious adverse events and selected predefined categories.
